items.summary: Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL), IBM and AMD launched a co-design platform for quantum error correction at IBM's site in Poughkeepsie, New York. The U.S. Department of Energy's Quantum Science Center (QSC) at ORNL and AMD are its inaugural partners. The platform pairs IBM Quantum Nighthawk r2 processors with Umbra, QSC's high-performance computing system built on AMD Instinct MI355X GPUs and 5th Gen AMD EPYC CPUs. It lets researchers develop quantum algorithms without building infrastructure themselves. Experiments have run up to 70 logical qubits through 438 difficult operations, a roughly 230-fold jump toward the Genesis Mission's Q Competition target of 100 logical qubits running 100,000 such operations by late 2028.
items.title: ORNL, IBM and AMD Launch Quantum Error Correction Co-Design Platform

items.summary: Hogwarts Legacy received an NVIDIA DLSS 5 upgrade with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering today, bringing lifelike lighting and materials to the game when streamed through GeForce NOW. The update adds detailed visuals while retaining underlying geometry and textures, tuned by Avalanche Software via DLSS 5 developer controls. It also supports DLSS Multi Frame Generation and Ray Reconstruction for enhanced ray-traced graphics. Published by Warner Bros., developed by Avalanche Software under the Portkey Games label, Hogwarts Legacy is an open-world action role-playing game set in the 1800s wizarding world.
items.title: NVIDIA Adds DLSS 5 Support to Hogwarts Legacy on GeForce NOW

items.summary: The podcast asks whether Elon Musk was the US midterms' biggest loser after spending $446m dollars on Republican-aligned political action committees. Democrats won every one of the five Senate races where his America PAC spent most, and hosts Blake Montgomery joined Carter Sherman to discuss what a Democratic wave means for tech.
items.title: Musk's Midterm Spending Called a Poor Investment for Tech

items.summary: At its developer conference on Thursday, Box unveiled a feature called Box Content Retrieval that embeds Nvidia's Nemotron embedding system into the core of its product. Nvidia VP Kari Briski told TechCrunch she expects queries answered four times faster, with 20% fewer errors and 90% fewer tokens used. The system will reach Enterprise Advance customers early next year.
items.title: Box Integrates Nvidia’s Nemotron Into Agent-First Content Retrieval

items.summary: mm2 Asia (mm2A), the former operator of Cathay Cineplexes, said in a bourse filing on Nov 5 that its proposed restructuring scheme for itself and subsidiary mm2 Entertainment (mm2E) was approved by creditors. The group must now seek court sanction under the Companies Act to proceed. Shares were suspended from trading since Nov 11, 2025, while moratoria protection remains in place until Nov 21, 2026.
items.title: Ex-Cathay Cineplex Operator mm2 Asia Wins Creditor Approval for Restructuring Scheme

items.summary: The Bank of England raised interest rates on Nov 5, the first increase in over three years, voting 8-1 to lift rates to 4% from 3.75%. Governor Andrew Bailey said at least one more rise was likely if a Middle East conflict continued, though he warned it would not be inevitable or necessarily final. British inflation is projected to reach around 5% by mid-2027, well above the central bank's target. The Bank also revised up growth forecasts for 2026 and 2027 while projecting inflation peaking at an average of 4.8% in early 2027 under its central scenario.
items.title: Bank of England Raises Interest Rates for First Time Since 2023

items.summary: HRL Laboratories, an IBM company, has developed a new inertial measurement unit (IMU) using micro-electromechanical systems (MEMS) sensors to provide uninterruptible navigation as an alternative to satellite-based global positioning system (GPS), which can be disrupted by tall buildings, the deep ocean, or electronic interference. The device uses dead reckoning and is about the size of a soup can, making it suitable for lightweight vehicles like aerial drones. Its key innovation is AutoCal, a self-calibrating system that solves bias drift to enable indefinite navigation use. HRL aims to shrink the IMU further toward hockey-puck size and expects production to begin in 2027.
items.title: HRL Develops GPS-Rivaling MEMS Inertial Navigation System

items.summary: In an opinion piece dated Nov 5, 2026, Nathalie Maréchal frames Tuesday's Democratic electoral gains as a rejection of what she calls the tech oligarchy and its allies. She argues that despite these results, technofascism persists and demands accountability through congressional investigations into executive-branch wrongdoing rather than retribution. Maréchal warns that reform will be hamstrung by the White House until 2029, when a new administration takes office in January. She urges structural reforms targeting tech industry power—wealth, data, market concentration—and calls for dismantling Silicon Valley's surveillance-based business models as essential work before broader renewal can follow.
items.title: Columnist Calls for Accountability After Left's Electoral Gains

items.summary: Snap settled its Los Angeles Superior Court case over Snapchat’s design just days after Meta, following earlier settlements by TikTok and YouTube, with terms kept confidential. Plaintiffs alleged deliberate addictive design caused harm to young users. The cases came from a JCCP consolidating thousands of claims; the first bellwether trial found Meta and Google liable for $6 million in damages (Meta is appealing). Experts note settlements may limit policy discussion and reduce data on how juries will rule, though one attorney said they signal companies take litigation risk seriously. Confidential terms remain undisclosed.
items.title: Social Media Addiction Trials Settle Before Verdict

items.summary: Engineers at NVIDIA and Databricks built a sink that lets teams push change data capture from PostgreSQL directly into Unity Catalog–governed Delta tables without an intermediate Kafka cluster. The open-source contribution, shipped in the Debezium Server 3.7 release, pairs with Debezium’s log tailing to stream events straight into the lakehouse while keeping database ownership under the team that runs it. NVIDIA added envelope mode, landing each full change event in a fixed nine-column table with idempotency keys and durable acknowledgment for at-least-once delivery. A companion blog walks through building a current-state Type-1 table using AUTO CDC sequenced by source LSN.
items.title: NVIDIA and Databricks Add Zerobus Ingest Sink for Debezium

items.summary: Shaun Goh, Director Manpower at the Ministry of Defence and Singapore Armed Forces (SAF), responds to Patrick Tan's letter urging a review of women serving in national service. He states that today enlisting male citizens meets defence needs, so there is no critical need to enlist women for NS. Women still contribute as SAF regulars, through the Volunteer Corps, and via SG Defence.
items.title: Defence official says conscription should follow critical need

items.summary: Gradium launched Phonon, a small text-to-speech model that runs on-device with no server or network required. The team announced it in April and spent six months building the release with partners and early users. Phonon comes in two sizes of about 65 MB and 75 MB and speaks English, French, German, Spanish and Portuguese through more than 100 built-in voices plus voice cloning. It is open: Phonon 31m runs under an Apache 2. 0 license for commercial use, while the other models are non-commercial (CC BY-NC). On Hugging Face's Open TTS Leaderboard, across 23 languages, Phonon ranks first in German and Spanish and places in the top three in every language evaluated, next to models up to 100 times its size. It also tops the CPU streaming benchmark on time-to-first audio. The team built a new inference framework called ptts supporting more than 10 backends.
items.title: Phonon Launches Open On-Device Text-to-Speech Model

items.summary: Australia’s Reserve Bank lifted interest rates to an 18-year high, citing growing “inflationary pressures” partly driven by datacentre-related investment. Governor Michele Bullock said some pain now could prevent worse pain later but admitted the timing of AI benefits is uncertain. Deloitte Access Economics reported a $141bn pipeline including 37 datacentres, up 36% in a year. Shadow energy minister Dan Tehan called green subsidies a “blowout” from $2.3bn to $8.5bn. US midterms showed voters opposing nearby datacentres and treating AI as major factors, suggesting the Albanese government should tread carefully while considering alternatives beyond monetary policy.
items.title: RBA datacentre inflation warning prompts Labor caution

items.summary: Apoorv Shankar, a former Ultrahuman vice president of hardware, is unveiling the Aina Ring to let users quickly approve or reject AI agent actions without pulling out their phones. The company has been in stealth for 15 months and debuted experimental products at CES 2026 under Project Mirage before announcing the ring today. Preorders are live now at $399 for a limited time, with the retail price rising to $499 when shipping begins in January 2027. Shankar says approvals will become central to future interfaces and that display confirmation is essential so users can trust devices.
items.title: Aina Unveils Smart Ring for Approving AI Agent Actions

items.summary: As countries negotiate legal wording at COP31 in Antalya, Turkey – with Australia jointly running talks as president of negotiations – Carbon Brief has launched a searchable interactive text tracker. The tool decodes the agenda and records each document by topic, date, page count and link to the original PDFs. It currently counts 104 substantive items on the agenda, excluding procedural matters such as electing officials. Each item is colour-coded in traffic-light format: red for no paper yet, orange for informal drafts, yellow once a draft legal text appears (with brackets marking disagreement), green when agreement is reached, and grey where talks are postponed under rule 16.
items.title: Carbon Brief launches real-time tracker for COP31 negotiating texts

items.summary: After Tuesday's election, Democrats flipped control of governors' offices in Georgia, Iowa, Ohio, Nevada and Texas, erasing Republicans' prior advantage over state legislative seats. Analysts say the shift clears a path for more climate legislation; Caroline Spears of Climate Cabinet called it "a generational political window" to lower costs and pollution while addressing inflation-driven energy prices. Jay Inslee urged lawmakers to seize the opportunity, calling President Trump "the election's clear loser." John Farrell of the Institute for Local Self-Reliance sees chances to rein in utility rates, noting renewed public scrutiny makes old campaign-finance tactics less likely to succeed.
items.title: Democrats' Statehouse Gains Open Climate Policy Path

items.summary:
Intel is diverting CPU manufacturing capacity from personal computers toward enterprise artificial intelligence infrastructure, confirmed during its recent quarterly earnings call. Rising memory prices and weakening consumer demand are pressuring the PC market, which Intel expects to remain slow through at least the first half of 2027. CEO Lip-Bu Tan stated that demand for Xeon CPUs remains robust despite near-term headwinds across the industry.

visual {
items.title: Intel Redirects Chip Capacity From PCs To AI Infrastructure Amid Industry Slowdown

items.summary: Content management firm Box expanded its partnership with Nvidia on Thursday (Nov 5), unveiling a search engine and an AI workflow builder for Enterprise Advanced customers. The company said the new tool could improve search accuracy by 20 per cent, cut token usage by 90 per cent, and speed up question-answering fourfold.
items.title: Box Expands Nvidia Partnership, Unveils AI Workflow Builder

items.summary: On November 5, IBM, AMD and Oak Ridge National Laboratory launched a joint platform pairing IBM's quantum computers with ORNL's Umbra supercomputer to test methods for detecting and correcting errors in quantum computing. The effort supports the US Department of Energy goal of building a scientifically useful quantum computer by late 2028. IBM said ongoing experiments are roughly 230 times short of that target, while it plans to invest more than $10 billion as it aims to build its first large-scale quantum computer by 2029.
items.title: IBM, AMD and ORNL Launch Quantum Error Correction Platform

items.summary: OpenAI launched the Images 2.6 model, letting users turn photos or text into animated GIFs with adjustable speed (0.5x to 2x) and per-frame edits without video software. It is available in India on free and paid ChatGPT plans.
items.title: OpenAI Unveils ChatGPT’s Images 2.6 for Animated GIFs

items.summary: In a VoxDevTalks episode, Michael Peters discusses new research presented at the 2026 STEG conference in Nairobi on service-led economic growth. He argues that many fast-growing developing economies have bypassed industrialisation, with workers moving from agriculture into local consumer services such as retail, hospitality, and small-scale transport rather than factories. New structural estimates suggest productivity gains in these services genuinely raised incomes, but because the services are consumed mainly by wealthy city-dwellers, benefits concentrate among urban households. Peters notes that India's consumer-facing services account for around 20% of private sector employment versus about 12% for manufacturing, and raises open questions about disguised unemployment and South Africa's roughly 30% unemployment rate before suggesting formalisation could help poorer workers.
items.title: Service-led growth may outpace factories in developing economies

items.summary: A study by E. Kipchumba (2026) evaluates the Disability-Inclusive Ultra-Poor Graduation (DIG) programme, a BRAC-run adaptation of an ultra-poor graduation model in four districts of Northern Uganda. The trial covered 185 community clusters and roughly 3,400 households, measuring impacts about 18 months after the programme ended. DIG helped participants with disabilities move from casual paid work into farming, raising named-participant farming participation by about 20 percentage points. However, attitudes did not improve: overall attendance at social events rose 12%, but only among respondents without a disabled household member, and one prejudice measure may have worsened. The author notes the trial cannot isolate what drove attitude change because economic and social components were delivered together (s41). Policy implications include including people with disabilities in such programmes and tackling prejudice directly (s46–s47).
items.title: Uganda graduation programme lifted incomes but not attitudes toward disability

items.summary: OpenAI announced Thursday it will cover all electricity and infrastructure expenses at future data center campuses it owns and operates, a move aimed at easing growing political backlash against AI data centers and the technology overall.
items.title: OpenAI to Cover Data Center Costs Amid Political Backlash

items.summary: Agility Robotics began trading on Nasdaq Thursday, becoming the first publicly listed pure-play humanoid robotics company with active commercial deployments, per the company. Its stock and warrants trade under symbols AGLT and AGLTW after a business combination that raised about $465 million in gross capital before expenses, including roughly $201 million from a Foxconn-led investment and $100 million of earlier equity funding, according to Bloomberg. Agility plans to use proceeds for customer orders, deployments, Digit production and its physical AI platform; it said Digit 5 has attracted committed multi-year orders worth more than $300 million, subject to contractual milestones.
items.title: Agility Robotics Lists on Nasdaq as First U.S. Humanoid Robot Public Company

items.summary: A Federal Reserve Bank of New York Liberty Street Economics post argues the U.S. oil sector restrained prices after an early-2026 Middle East conflict caused an unprecedented drop in global petroleum supply, though prices did not reach unprecedented highs. Drilling had created oversupply beforehand; inventories filled half the second-quarter gap by some estimates but stopped falling in July, so other countries absorbed the shortfall—China notably cut imports sharply since April. The author notes electrification may bring forward the year of declining global oil demand and that outcomes depend on how the conflict resolves. Figures are drawn from EIA estimates; views are those of the author(s) only.
items.title: U.S. Oil Output Helped Ease Middle East Supply Shock

items.summary: Beijing called on the US and EU to reconsider tariffs on Chinese goods, coinciding with record-high exports. Beijing said it would buy more American farm products only if both sides cut duties, though restarted soybean imports remain well below pre-trade-war levels. Officials also urged Brussels to review new measures targeting low-value retail imports from Shein and Temu.
items.title: China Urges US and EU to Reconsider Tariffs Amid Record Exports

items.summary: A FRED graph compares two U.S. Census retail trade sales series, showing that summing the 12 monthly values of the Monthly Retail Trade Survey yields a year total within a few million dollars of the more comprehensive Annual Integrated Economic Survey (AIES) annual figure: about $7.107 trillion for 2024. The AIES serves as a foundational benchmark with a large sample, revising faster surveys and updating the Census Business Register; other agencies apply similar methods to GDP, producer prices, productivity, and industrial production.
items.title: The Census Recalibrates Retail Sales Data With Its Annual Survey

items.summary: The Bank of England’s base-rate increase leaves most borrowers unaffected, as more than 7.3m (87%) of Britain’s almost 8.5m existing residential mortgages are fixed rate. Around 510,000 tracker-mortgage holders will see payments rise in line with the hike; UK Finance says a typical customer owes £147,000 and could pay £30.72 more monthly. Some of the 470,000 borrowers on standard variable rates may also pay more, though lenders are not obliged to pass it on fully (UK Finance estimates about £14.28 a month). New mortgage deals have reached a three-year high of 5.89%, per Moneyfacts. Nicholas Mendes at John Charcol says several big lenders cut fixed-deal costs earlier this week. For savers, easy-access rates averaged 2.58% on Thursday morning, with best-buy accounts up to 5%. Katie Horne at Flagstone added that a single 0.25% rise is unlikely to move fixed savings much further.
items.title: UK rate rise and its effect on mortgages and savings

items.summary: The Bank of England has raised interest rates to 4% and signalled more increases may follow, though the rate-setting committee is split on how many. Three members cited multiple rises while one voted for a larger jump to 4. 25%; three, including governor Andrew Bailey, called for just one further rise in February. The Bank's forecasts point to inflation near 5% as household energy bills surge by 27% to £2,150 annually amid an ongoing war and oil averaging $108 a barrel, though the economy has outperformed expectations with growth of 0. 6%, 0. 5% and projected 0. 7%.
items.title: Bank of England signals further interest-rate rises amid uncertain outlook

items.summary: A CGTN commentator argues that this year's ninth China International Import Expo in Shanghai is judged by how quickly debuts become purchases rather than foot traffic. More than 480 representative products are making their debut, a record high; clearance for imported consumer goods has been cut from at least seven days to same-day release. May 2025 measures let small batches of up to 20 units clear with no waiting. The eighth CIIE recorded an intention-based transaction value of $83.49 billion on an annualized basis, up 4.4%, a record high, with cumulative deals exceeding $500 billion over eight editions. Brands such as Limar and Blé de Fonty are cited as examples of faster shelf access. The piece notes that unless hall interest turns into sales, commercial value fades. It concludes the speed from exhibits to products signals China's market vitality. (Note: figures retained exactly as written.)
items.title: Shanghai's CIIE Pushes Faster Turn of Exhibits Into Sales

items.summary: On The Hub, Wang Guan interviews Wayne Brown, mayor of Auckland, New Zealand, at the 2026 Global Mayors Dialogue in Ningbo. Brown discusses how openness and connectivity can drive shared growth between cities. He explores cooperation from Auckland learning from Ningbo's port efficiency to city-to-city exchanges, tech innovation and cross-sector collaboration. Brown also champions open trade over protectionism and explains how connectivity improves urban life.
items.title: Auckland Mayor Wayne Brown on Openness and Connectivity in Cities

items.summary: Wang Huning, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and chairman of the CPPCC National Committee, urged members of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC) to study and implement guiding principles from the Fifth Plenary Session of the 20th Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee. He called thorough implementation a major political task for 2027 work in Beijing.
items.title: Wang Huning Urges CPPCC to Implement CPC Plenum Principles

items.summary: A Beihang University team is designing a conceptual road on the moon, made from crushed stone excavated in situ or sintered there. Professor Li Feng told CGTN that modern roads began as gravel surfaces, so the lunar version could follow suit. The Qinzhidao concept honors an ancient Chinese highway over 2,200 years old. Published January 2026 in the China Journal of Highway and Transport.
items.title: Beihang University Team Designs Concept for China's First Lunar Road

items.summary: The National Development and Reform Commission, with the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology and three other departments, issued an action plan to promote resource conservation and accelerate China's green transition. It targets reducing energy consumption per unit of GDP by around 10%, water use by 10%, and construction land use by 15% by 2030 from 2025 levels, plus raising recyclable-resource recycling to 510 million tonnes annually by 2030. NDRC's Li Zhong said the measures support carbon peaking before 2030 and neutrality before 2060.
items.title: China Unveils Resource Conservation Action Plan

items.summary: Five unions launched a national day of strike action across France, joining high-school students and demonstrators over the rising cost of living. More than 250,000 people had taken to the streets in almost 70 towns by Thursday afternoon, according to CGT's Sophie Binet, who said it was only
items.title: French Unions Launch National Strike Amid Rising Living Costs

items.summary: The Transport Workers Union has condemned a proposed policy that would let passengers carry firearms in personal lock boxes aboard US intercity trains. TWU International staff representative Brian Delucia said the plan covers an additional 1,500 trains a day across the country. The union says many stations lack staff or police to respond if something goes wrong and called on the federal government to reverse course before it begins January 2027. Amtrak did not immediately comment.
items.title: TWU Condemns Amtrak’s Plan to Allow Guns on Trains

items.summary: Russell Brand has been found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault, the court reported. The comedian and actor, 51, was remanded in custody and will be sentenced on Monday. The charges date from 1999 to 2009 and concerned six women who are all entitled to lifelong anonymity.
items.title: Russell Brand Found Guilty of Rape and Sexual Assault

items.summary: A jury found Russell Brand guilty of four offences, including one rape charge, after a four-week trial at Southwark crown court. He had pleaded not guilty to charges spanning 10 years from 1999 against six women. Justice Bennathan told him he would be remanded in custody and sentenced on Monday. Police praised the victims for coming forward despite intense scrutiny.
items.title: Russell Brand Convicted of Rape and Sexual Assault

items.summary: Residents of Tumucumaque Indigenous Park in Amapá state, northern Brazil, could not vote in the October general elections because they had no local polling station and lacked transport to Macapá. Mitore Tiriyo Kaxuyana, a leader of the Tiriyó and Kaxuyana peoples who spoke with Mongabay, said officials there were unaware the territory existed. The park holds 74 villages and about 2,800 citizens across five municipalities in two states. A technical note from advisers at the Ministry of Indigenous Peoples seen by Mongabay found roughly 26% of Brazil's Indigenous voters didn't vote in October, above the 20% average for all eligible Brazilian voters.
items.title: Remote Indigenous Territory in Brazil Was Left Out of October Elections

items.summary: Public health researchers, including Franklin Glozah, examined gambling across sub-Saharan Africa and argue the issue is framed too narrowly as addiction. Industry estimates suggest annual betting revenue could rise from US$3.5 billion in 2021 to US$19.4 billion by 2030. A 2026 survey of 2,866 people across six countries found that 64% in Kenya, 60% in Ghana and 54% in Nigeria bet on football in the preceding year; among active bettors, 95% used mobile devices. Glozah notes gambling may offer a source of income amid economic insecurity and links attitudes to social support rather than individual failing. He calls for regulation that addresses advertising and youth unemployment alongside responsible-gambling messaging.
items.title: Researchers Reframe Youth Sports Betting in Africa Beyond Addiction

items.summary: Researchers at the University of Zambia examined whether foreign aid origin affects household food security in eastern Zambia. Surveying over 545 smallholder households in Chipata and Mambwe districts since 2014, they found donor affiliation made little difference to outcomes. Local farming practices mattered more: conservation agriculture improved food security by reducing climate risk and boosting yields, while Chinese-backed cotton contract farming reduced crop diversity and increased vulnerability. Female-headed households faced lower dietary diversity due to cultural norms restricting land access.
items.title: Zambian Study Finds Local Farming, Not Donor Aid, Drives Food Security

items.summary: Ghana became the first African country awarded a Forest Law Enforcement, Governance and Trade (FLEGT) license, seen as the “gold standard” in sustainable timber trade and enabling EU market access. Author Chris Beeko, Ghana’s VPA focal point and former Forestry Commission director, argues the deeper legacy lies in how the Voluntary Partnership Agreement process reformed national institutions. After a 16-year journey, it integrated forest-sector agencies under one legality system (GhLAS) and brought government, industry and civil society to shared governance. Beeko cautions against judging success only by licenses issued, noting forests face broader pressures like agricultural expansion.
items.title: Ghana’s FLEGT License Marks a Governance Turning Point

items.summary: After US Democrats won control of both chambers in the midterms, analysts weigh how this affects strained US-India ties. The immediate test is trade: an interim framework discussed by Trump and Prime Minister Narendra Modi remains unformalized over market access. Shanthie Mariet D'Souza expects increased scrutiny of protectionist measures but says strategic partnership pillars will hold. Immigration tensions persist after the administration's $100,000 (€88,761) H-1B fee; lawyer Rajkrishna Iyer predicts courts may strike it down. Disputes over Russian oil and a $686 million US arms sale to Pakistan for F-16 jets continue. Experts remain divided on whether Trump will moderate or double down as his term nears its end in 2026.
items.title: US Democrats' midterm win and its uncertain impact on US-India relations

items.summary: The Up First newsletter previews what lies ahead for Democrats following midterm election results in which the party won several districts and states President Trump carried by double digits two years earlier. It now holds its largest Senate majority since passage of the Affordable Care Act, though Alaska and Mississippi returns remain pending. NPR's Tamara Keith notes that uncalled House races still linger but says the Democratic swing already rivals the post-Watergate era. With a new Congress unlikely to pass major legislation, leaders plan ambitious investigations instead.
items.title: What's next for Democrats after the midterms. And, a look at the outstanding races

items.summary: UCLA experts argue fireworks pose underestimated public health risks, prompting calls for stronger regulation and education. They cite severe burns, blast and brain injuries, amputations and blindness, which disproportionately affect children and bystanders. In the Netherlands an estimated 1,239 people needed emergency treatment during New Year's celebrations in 2025-2026, a 7% rise from the previous year.
items.title: Experts urge stricter firework rules amid rising European injuries

items.summary: The liquidation of Ueno Bank, detected after its solvency ratio fell below 50%, triggered Paraguay's worst institutional crisis in years. Around three million customers were frozen when the bank closed on Tuesday 3 November, holding about 850 million dollars (about 758 million euros) in public resources, including pension and healthcare funds from the Instituto de Previsión Social. Crowds gathered outside its branches as fears of a corralito spread. The political opposition blames BCP leadership by omission; at the request of 35 legislators, the Chamber of Deputies will meet to vote on impeachment against President Santiago Peña, requiring 53 votes and two-thirds Senate backing. Charges include conflict of interest and alleged embezzlement of pension funds. Eight executives were arrested, including chief executive Miguel Vázquez.
items.title: Paraguay Moves Toward Impeaching Peña After Ueno Bank Collapse

items.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) implemented a uniform $5 million limit on outstanding positions in rupee-related currency derivatives for domestic clients and foreign portfolio investors across all relevant pairs and exchanges, without requiring underlying exposure. The change aligns with the Reserve Bank of India's revised thresholds announced on 10 October, replacing earlier provisions that had set the limit at $100 million.
items.title: Sebi Aligns Rupee Derivative Limits With RBI Threshold

items.summary: The page opens with Dhanteras, also called Dhantrayodashi, described as the start of the Diwali festivities and an auspicious time to welcome wealth. It notes that the festival is celebrated with prayers, diyas and buying precious metals, bringing families together in hope. The item then invites readers to share English wishes, quotes and WhatsApp status messages with loved ones to spread festive cheer.
items.title: Dhanteras Wishes Shared Ahead of Diwali

items.summary: Microsoft has declined an option to lease additional computing capacity at its Ward County, Texas data centre for AI start-up Nscale, according to people familiar with the matter cited by the Financial Times. The decision may force Nscale to seek new customers or risk losing billions in potential revenue as it prepares for a possible $35 billion IPO this year.
items.title: Microsoft Passes on Expanding Nscale Texas Deal

items.summary: On November 4, election-related queries dominated Google's top searches in the United States, with “Alaska Senate race” leading and “Habibi meaning” reaching the top 10. The term gained attention after newly elected Democratic Senator Abdul El-Sayed used it during his victory speech, addressing Vice President JD Vance as “habibi.” Democrats also made gains, holding at least 54 of 100 Senate seats and flipping at least 30 House seats for a total of 240. Source: Deccan Chronicle.
items.title: Google Search Trends Follow US Midterm Election Results

items.summary: The Students Federation of India (SFI), the student wing of the CPM, lodged a complaint with President Droupadi Murmu against Keralam Governor O.P. Mathur over his Instagram handle "ommathurbjp." SFI Thiruvananthapuram district secretary Nandan M.A. stated that associating the constitutional office with a political party violates neutrality and could erode public trust in institutions.
items.title: SFI Complaint Against BJP Tag on Kerala Governor's Instagram Handle

items.summary: Meta has joined Google and Microsoft by offering voluntary exit options (VEOs) to staff in France, with a November 5 application deadline. According to La Lettre, roughly 100 of the company's ~300 French employees may be affected. Unlike its rivals' individual offers, Meta uses RCC, a collective contractual termination procedure under French labour law. Participants receive about 2.15 months' salary per year of service plus 10 months of paid leave at 80% gross pay. The move follows April layoffs of ~8,000 roles (~10%) and May reassignments of ~7,000 staff to AI-linked functions, alongside projected capital expenditure between $135 billion and $145 billion in 2026.
items.title: Meta Extends Voluntary Exit Program in France Amid AI-Driven Cuts

items.summary: A Europinion report says the delay in Elon Musk's Starlink launch in India comes from pending regulatory and security approvals rather than obstruction by domestic telecom companies, as Musk had alleged. The Indian government called the claim baseless. The report notes both Reliance Jio and Bharti Airtel signed distribution agreements, that spectrum pricing was approved but final clearance is still pending, and that over 11,000 villages lacked 4G connectivity as of May 2026.
items.title: Report Questions Musk's Claims of Telecom Blocking Starlink in India

items.summary: Meta has joined Google and Microsoft by offering voluntary exits to some employees, starting with France under a collective process called RCC that bargains with trade unions. About 100 of Meta's roughly 300 French staff could be affected; interested workers must apply by November 5. Under the proposed terms, employees would receive 2.15 months' salary per year worked plus 80% of gross pay for ten months of mobility leave. It is unclear whether other roles or countries will follow.
items.title: Meta Joins Google and Microsoft in Offering Voluntary Exits

items.summary: The Election Commission clarified that Seema Khanna's supervisory authority remains unchanged after a poll panel revised her work allocation, placing her under deputy election commissioner Prakash Raj Purohit. The clarification followed an order by Manish Garg and objections from commissioners Sandhu and Joshi over centralized powers in electoral roll software controlled by the EC's IT division.
items.title: Election Commission Confirms Unchanged Reporting Line for IT Chief Khanna

items.summary: Union minister Chirag Paswan mocked Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav for saying he would not contest the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, comparing him to a commander watching soldiers fight from a palace. Asked if Yadav feared defeat or worried about party performance, Paswan cited Maharashtra's 2024 results and noted BJP won only 33 of UP's 80 Lok Sabha seats in 2024 versus SP's 37.
items.title: Paswan Mocks Yadav Over UP Polls Remark

items.summary: A research report by Emkay Research says Donald Trump's electoral setback in the 2026 midterm elections could ease trade-related pressure on India and give New Delhi more room to negotiate favourable terms with Washington. The Democrats' victory may limit aggressive tariff moves, though Trade remains one of few areas he controls alone.
items.title: Emkay Research Sees Eased Tariff Pressure on India After Trump Midterm Setback

items.summary: The Bombay Natural History Society published the book Mammals of India with Harper Collins Publishers India, authored by A.J.T. Johnsingh and P.O. Nameer. Johnsingh died in 2024 before publication. In an interview conducted by Mongabay-India, Nameer recounts that the project began in 2018 to serve both researchers and general readers, explaining how geological history shaped India's mammalian diversity.
items.title: BNHS Releases Mammals of India Book With Co-Author's Death

items.summary: The government has taken over the Air Force Sports Complex near Lok Kalyan Marg as part of a land reclamation exercise. The facility, which includes a golf course and swimming pool, was governed by serving officers per a 2024 court judgment. Its closure disrupted an event for retiring Air Chief Marshal A P Singh. Other nearby properties, including the Delhi Race Club and Jaipur Polo Ground, were also reclaimed.
items.title: Government Takes Over Delhi Air Force Sports Complex in Land Reclamation Drive

items.summary: Initial claims for state unemployment benefits fell 6,000 to a seasonally adjusted 189,000 for the week ended October 31, matching mid-July and marking the lowest reading since 1969. Claims stayed mostly below 200,000 since September as low layoffs from strong domestic demand anchored the labor market. Andy Challenger of Challenger, Gray & Christmas said employers are retaining workers heading into holidays with largely short-term hiring. Continuing claims rose to 1.718 million for the week ended October 24 but exclude some unemployed people. The report has no bearing on Friday's employment data as it falls outside the survey period.
items.title: US Jobless Claims Fall to Lowest Level Since 1969

items.summary:
The Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) disclosed in an RTI response that the building which collapsed on September 6, killing seven people and injuring others, had neither a sanctioned plan nor a completion certificate. The MCD said it received no complaints about unauthorised construction or structural safety before the incident and issued no inspection report, sealing order or demolition notice for the adjoining Hostel Daze property. It did not confirm whether the building was classified as illegal, nor provide licence details, an inspection register or ATRs. Separately, Delhi Police filed a chargesheet against six people under culpable homicide not amounting to murder and other Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita sections.
